controls.title: AI management system scope and leadership commitment
controls.summary: Leadership has defined the scope of the AI management system and demonstrates visible commitment to responsible AI practices.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a documented scope statement and evidence of leadership involvement (e.g. steering committee), not just a policy PDF.

controls.title: AI risk assessment methodology
controls.summary: The vendor has a documented, repeatable methodology for identifying and assessing risks specific to AI systems, distinct from general IT risk assessment.
controls.validationGuidance: The methodology should address AI-specific risks (bias, hallucination, misuse) rather than reusing a generic IT risk framework unmodified.

controls.title: AI objectives and roles
controls.summary: The organization has defined measurable AI management objectives and assigned clear roles and responsibilities for achieving them.
controls.validationGuidance: Objectives should be specific and measurable, not aspirational statements like 'use AI responsibly.'

controls.title: Competence and awareness of personnel working with AI
controls.summary: Personnel involved in developing, deploying, or overseeing AI systems have appropriate training on responsible AI practices and system limitations.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for role-specific training (e.g. for ML engineers vs. business users), not a single generic awareness module.

controls.title: Documented information and version control for AI systems
controls.summary: The vendor maintains version-controlled documentation of AI system design, training data provenance, and configuration changes over time.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm documentation is kept current with deployed versions, not just accurate for an initial release.

controls.title: AI system lifecycle controls (design through decommissioning)
controls.summary: The vendor applies defined controls at each stage of the AI system lifecycle, including design, development, validation, deployment, and eventual decommissioning.
controls.validationGuidance: Decommissioning is a commonly overlooked stage - check whether retired models and their training data are handled with the same care as active ones.

controls.title: Data quality and provenance controls for training data
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to ensure training and fine-tuning data is fit for purpose, appropriately sourced, and free of known contamination or bias issues where feasible.
controls.validationGuidance: This is difficult to fully verify for third-party/foundation models - look for at least a documented data sourcing policy.

controls.title: Impact assessment for AI systems affecting individuals
controls.summary: Before deployment, the vendor assesses potential impacts of the AI system on individuals or groups, including fairness and access considerations.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for this being a gating step before deployment, not a post-hoc review after complaints arise.

controls.title: Performance evaluation and internal audit of the AI management system
controls.summary: The organization periodically evaluates the effectiveness of its AI management system, including through internal audit or equivalent review.
controls.validationGuidance: A recent internal audit report or independent assessment is stronger evidence than a stated intention to audit.

controls.title: Continual improvement and corrective action process
controls.summary: The vendor has a defined process for identifying nonconformities in its AI management system and taking corrective action, with evidence of past use.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for an example of the process being used, not just its existence on paper.
